**Finding: compliant (no redline proposed).**

The Agreement contains no audit right running against Sparkling. I checked every plausible location:

- **§ 3 Restrictions on Use** (p0029–p0037) — substantive use limits only (no copying, no reverse engineering, no sublicensing, precautions against third-party misuse); no licence-verification or inspection right.
- **§ 9 Co-operation** (p0060) — Sparkling's project manager provides information "as Garman may reasonably require in order to perform its obligations hereunder," i.e. implementation co-operation, not a verification audit.
- **§ 10 Maintenance and Support** — support/access flows *to* Sparkling, not audit access for Garman.
- **§ 14 Confidentiality** (p0095) — refers to accounting records only as a category of Confidential Information; grants no inspection right.
- **§ 20 / Page 10 general matters** (p0134–p0147) — notices, waiver, assignment, independent contractor, force majeure, severability, governing law, headings; no audit clause.

Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect/verify/compliance", "access", "records", "premises/books", "monitor usage/licence verification" and "Garman may / shall have the right" returned nothing responsive.

Because no audit obligation binds us, the position is stronger than the preferred checklist (which exists only to constrain such a right). Inserting frequency, notice and cost-allocation limits would require first creating an audit right against ourselves, which would weaken our position — so this is recorded as compliant with no proposed changes.
